assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential account of how technology, tasks and trade shocks reshape employment and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for the task and trade-shock contributions.
assessment.maturity: The research has been influential across labour, trade and policy for many years and has generated extensive subsequent evidence.
uncertainties: The contribution joins distinct technology and trade-shock literatures, making the precise prize citation difficult to delimit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data evidence transformed measurement and understanding of intergenerational mobility.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the collaborative empirical mobility programme.
assessment.maturity: Its methods, data construction and findings have had durable academic and public-policy influence.
uncertainties: The candidate's four-person credit set requires exclusion of a major listed contributor under the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of theory and empirical measurement of selection in insurance markets has materially advanced applied welfare analysis.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie provide a well-defined set spanning empirical measurement and the relevant theoretical framework.
assessment.maturity: The work is established, broadly applied, and central to modern health and insurance economics.
uncertainties: The broader adverse-selection literature makes the boundary of a single discovery contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied practical identification and estimation tools used throughout empirical economics.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are closely associated with the central estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: These methods have been standard tools for decades, with a clear and lasting methodological legacy.
uncertainties: The methods' broad uptake does not by itself resolve questions about robustness in all applied settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed the discipline's approach to what data can credibly establish under limited assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the indispensable foundational figure for the central idea; a single-laureate proposal avoids overclaiming later extensions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and increasingly important for credible empirical inference.
uncertainties: The listed candidate combines foundational partial identification with later moment-inequality developments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of employer market power has reshaped labour-market measurement and policy debates.
assessment.attribution: Manning is central to the theoretical revival, while Ashenfelter and Naidu represent important empirical and institutional advances.
assessment.maturity: The topic has a substantial accumulated literature and clear relevance for wages and labour-market policy.
uncertainties: The causal magnitude and policy consequences of monopsony vary across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies made discrimination measurable in labour-market decisions and influenced empirical practice and policy.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to the landmark correspondence-study approach; Charles represents the wider labour-discrimination programme.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated across markets and countries and remains policy relevant.
uncertainties: Attributing an extensive audit-study tradition to this particular three-person grouping is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life shocks, child health and skill formation has established the economic importance of childhood conditions.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha make complementary contributions to empirical early-life research and dynamic skill-formation analysis.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated across cohorts, settings and policy applications.
uncertainties: The candidate links empirical early-life conditions with a broader structural skill-formation literature.
